facts: AES is a symmetric block cipher. Its block size is 128 bits.
SHA-256 produces a 256 bit message digest.
HMAC authenticates messages using a secret key and a hash function.
A nonce is a value intended to be used once within a defined protocol scope.
HKDF separates extract and expand stages for key derivation.
RSA uses a modulus that is the product of large prime numbers.
ECDSA signing requires a secret per-message scalar.
Ed25519 is a digital signature scheme.
ChaCha20 is a stream cipher built from addition rotation and XOR operations.
Poly1305 computes a message authentication tag.
GCM combines counter mode encryption with authentication.
A Merkle tree aggregates leaf hashes into a root hash.
A password salt differentiates otherwise identical password inputs.
Argon2 is a memory-hard password hashing function.
Forward secrecy limits exposure of past sessions after a long-term key compromise.
A key encapsulation mechanism establishes shared secret key material.
A zero knowledge proof can establish a statement without revealing its secret witness.
A commitment scheme has hiding and binding properties.
Secret sharing distributes shares so an authorized subset can reconstruct a secret.
